archetype.name: Pretender (special-teams propped)
archetype.definition: A Nashville side whose .500-plus points pace rests on an elite power play, an elite penalty kill and four overtime-loss points, while it is clearly outplayed at 5-on-5.

report.headline: Special teams are hiding a team losing badly at even strength
report.take:
Nashville is 4-3-4 with 12 points through 11 games. That sits it fourth in a crowded Central, and its 89-point pace would top last season's 86. The record looks like a bubble team holding its own. The underlying play says something less comfortable. At 5-on-5 the Predators own just 45.1% of the expected goals (26th) and 45% of the shot attempts (27th). They are getting out-possessed and out-chanced most nights, and the goal line follows: -0.36 a game, 21st in the league.

Two things keep the standings respectable. The power play converts 33.3% (3rd), about twelve points above the league's 21.2%. The penalty kill sits at 85.7% (5th). Stamkos (7 PP points), O'Reilly (6) and Josi (8) have done most of the scoring that way. Behind them, Juuse Saros is +3.0 GSAx with a .908, which earns the goaltending its B+ and covers for a blueline graded D. Add four overtime losses and a +1.1 Pts vs Goal Diff, and you get a team banking points it hasn't really controlled.

The numbers hide how lopsided the top of the lineup is at even strength. Stamkos (0.400 xGF %) and O'Reilly (0.403) lead the team in points while being badly out-chanced on the ice. Marchessault (0.341) and Hague (0.349) are worse. The six listed defensemen have one goal between them, and that came from Josi. There is one mild offset. The 5-on-5 PDO of 98.6 says the evens results have run a bit unlucky, so some even-strength scoring may come back even as the power play cools. History supports caution about that power play: it ran 17.6% to 24.4% over the last five seasons, never near a third of its chances.

The outlook is a team that drifts toward its 5-on-5 talent. That talent looks worse than last year's, when the team posted a 0.49 xGF % and missed the playoffs with 86 points. Unless the even-strength process improves, expect the points percentage to slide into the low-to-mid 80s point range as special teams normalize.

strengths.title: An elite, top-heavy power play
strengths.body: Nashville scores on a third of its power plays, third in the league and well above the league average. Stamkos, O'Reilly, Forsberg and Josi drive it. Some of the skill is real, since the unit ran 23.1% last year. But a rate this high almost always comes down over a full season.

strengths.title: Saros steadying the crease
strengths.body: Saros has started 8 of the 10 games the listed goalies have started, with a .908 and +3.0 GSAx. That carries a team GSAx ranked 11th and the group's B+. He has to keep it up, because Annunen has gone .846 in his two starts and the defense in front of both of them is a D.

strengths.title: A penalty kill punching above
strengths.body: The kill sits fifth at 85.7%, comfortably over the league's 78.3%. It has been one of the main reasons the team allows a near-league-average goals rate despite giving up more shots than it takes. The kill was solid last year at 81.7%, so a decent version of it should hold, though probably not at this level.

concerns.title: Outplayed at 5-on-5 most nights
concerns.body: A 45.1% expected-goals share and 45% of shot attempts both rank near the bottom of the league, a clear step down from last season's 0.49 xGF %. The stars are part of the problem: Stamkos and O'Reilly are leading the scoring while being out-chanced badly at evens. That is the kind of number that holds unless the lineup or the deployment changes.

concerns.title: A blueline with almost no support
concerns.body: Beyond Josi, the defense offers little. Six listed defensemen have one goal, and Perbix and Hunt have no points. Hague (0.349 xGF %) and Skjei (-6) are struggling in big minutes. This group earns the D grade and puts real weight on Saros.

concerns.title: Points the margin doesn't back
concerns.body: Four of the 11 games ended in overtime losses, which turned a losing goal line into a winning-looking points total. The team carries a +1.1 Pts vs Goal Diff and a -4 differential. Overtime coin flips even out, and the 82-game pace for the differential is -30.

trend.note: The results swing wildly, from a 0-6 loss in Boston to a 6-2 win over Colorado. The last 10 games (4-2-4, .600 points %) are only marginally better than the season as a whole. The rate of being out-chanced has not changed.

weekAhead.headline: Three home games, three tests for the power play
weekAhead.body:
All three games are in Nashville, against teams ranked 14th, 15th and 8th on the site, each a bit above the Predators' 17th. The Islanders are the low-event problem. They have elite goaltending (+8.9 GSAx, .914) and the league's fourth-best kill, which is exactly what blunts a team living off its power play. Washington is closer to even: a 47% Corsi side that allows shots, but its defense holds opposing defensemen down (3rd), so Josi's offense may have to come from elsewhere.

Tampa is the best team of the three by play, with a 56.4% expected-goals share and 30.4 shots a game. It will likely tilt the ice the way most opponents have against Nashville. Its weak spots fit what Nashville does well, though: a .884 team save % (23rd) and a 76.7% kill (19th). Two points out of three games would match the season's pace. Anything more probably needs the power play to stay hot.

keyMatchups.title: Predators PP vs Islanders PK
keyMatchups.body: Nashville's third-ranked power play meets a fourth-ranked kill backed by the league's third-best goaltending by GSAx. Even strength is unlikely to bail Nashville out here. If the power play is held quiet, a low-scoring game tilts toward the deeper five-on-five team.

keyMatchups.title: Tampa's leaky goaltending
keyMatchups.body: The Lightning out-chance nearly everyone, but their goalies carry a C- and a .884. Their kill is below average too. For a Nashville team that wins on special teams and opportunism, this is the best chance to steal a game against a better side.

keyMatchups.title: Josi against defense-friendly defenses
keyMatchups.body: The Islanders give extra points to defensemen (rank 24), while Washington is stingy there (rank 3). Josi is the blueline's only real source of offense, so the Islanders game is his opening. The Capitals game asks the forwards to carry more.

weekAhead.watch: Nashville's 5-on-5 shot share against Tampa: getting caved again by a top possession team would confirm the even-strength problem.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect the power play to come back toward the low-20s it has lived in historically, and the kill toward the low 80s. That removes the main cushion under this record. The overtime-loss points will also likely balance out. Working the other way, a 5-on-5 PDO of 98.6 points to some even-strength scoring bouncing back, and Saros playing like this keeps games close. The net is a team that finishes near or slightly below last season's 86 points, on the outside of a deep Central's playoff spots, unless the 45% shot share climbs back to the coin-flip territory of the last two years.

What is sustainable: Saros as an above-average starter, and a top six with enough skill to finish chances. What will regress: a power play near a third, overtime luck, and the stars' scoring pace while they are being out-chanced at evens.
swingFactors: How far the power play falls from a third
Whether Saros keeps a positive GSAx behind a D blueline
Any recovery in the top line's 5-on-5 xGF %

confidence.note: Eleven games is small, but the 5-on-5 share is lopsided enough to trust.
